newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends up but trade cautious ahead of elections.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends up but trade cautious ahead of elections.

text.p: Aided by a plethora of merger pacts that energized activity in individual shares, U.S. stocks ended stronger although investors were generally cautious ahead of Tuesday's elections.

"The markets are doing well prior to the election on the assumption (President Bill) Clinton will be re-elected and we'll have nothing worse than a narrowing of the majority in Congress that Republicans will have," said Allen Sinai, chief economist at Lehman Brothers Global Economic Advisors.
The Dow industrials rose 20 to about 6042.
With last week's 14.91 point gain, the blue chip index is nearing its all-time closing high of 6094.23 set October 18.
The S&P 500 index rose three to about 707.
Winners outpaced losers 13-10 on active NYSE volume of about 390 million shares.
But the Nasdaq Composite slipped one to about 1221.

The long bond rose 7/32 to yield 6.66 percent. "The bond market is poised to do better if the elections turn out okay," said Sinai, who projects a modest selloff should the Democrats take the White House and Congress. "At worst we have a selloff to 6-7/8 percent on the long bond" yield, he said.

Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management, said, "Bonds are concerned that a Democratic sweep will result in massive social spending and an upward explosion in the size of the deficit, which will drive inflation higher and bond prices lower."

But Sinai noted the fundamentals are still good for U.S. markets in general. "We have a slowdown in growth and quiet inflation showing up -- defining the lower trading range for interest rates." He also noted that the Dow "is not overvalued. It's the high end of fairly valued. Overvalued does not happen until we're north of 6200."
Other than the elections, Wall Street also paid some attention to the various announced "big deals," Orlando said.

MCI Communications rose 1/2 to 30-3/4 in the wake of news of a $20 billion plus merger with British Telecommunications. MCI shares traded well off a theoretical value that oscillated around $39 a share, based on BT's American depositary shares. MCI industry analysts cited regulatory hurdles for the deal and a lengthy 12 months to complete a pact as reasons why MCI was not trading higher. BT ADS surged 6-1/8 to 61-5/8.
AT&T lost 7/8 to 33-3/4 in the face of expected stronger competition from a merged MCI/BT.
Goldman Sachs downgraded AT&T to market underperform from market perform.

Norfolk Southern, up 1-1/4 to 90-3/4, said it is in talks with CSX Corp, up 1-7/8 to 44-7/8 about their respective offers to buy Conrail. Conrail lost 1-5/8 to 93-5/8 amid disappointment that a bidding war appeared less likely.
Southern National Corp, off 1-3/4 to 33-1/2, and United Carolina Bancshares, up 8-1/2 to 36, said their boards approved a stock-swap merger valued at $985 million.
Sierra Health Services, down five to 23-7/8, agreed to merge with Physician Corp of America, up 1/8 to 10-3/4.
On Sunday, J.C. Penney Co, off 1-7/8 to 51-1/8, and Eckerd Corp, up 4-1/2 to 33-1/4, said Penney will acquire Eckerd for cash and stock in a deal valued at about $3.3 billion.
Analysts said investors largely ignored news September construction spending rose 1.9 percent, the highest since a 2.3 percent gain in March. A 0.1 percent drop was expected.

Among individual shares, GM rose 1-5/8 to 55-5/8 as workers at a key metal stamping plant in Indianapolis returned to work Sunday after ratifying a deal to end a five-day strike that threatened to paralyze most of GM's light truck production. GM also set an unchanged quarterly dividend.
Micron rose 2-3/4 to 28 after Merrill upgraded the stock.
Foster Wheeler lost 4-5/8 to 35-3/8 after warning 1997 results would fall short of its 15 percent annual growth goal.

Dow component Texaco lost 2-1/8 to 97-5/8 after allegations of secret tape recordings of Texaco executives discussing destroying evidence in a discrimination lawsuit and disparaging minority workers. Texaco said it had retained outside counsel to investigate the allegations.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.30 to 1220.48.
The S&P 500 index rose 2.96 to 706.73.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721.
